cover.subtitle: Compliance with the ANSSI IT Hygiene Guide — the 42-rule framework, 2017 edition
cover.disclaimerBody: This document constitutes neither an ANSSI certification nor a legal opinion. It provides a technical mapping of the audited workstation's security posture against the ANSSI IT Hygiene Guide (42-rule reference framework).

overview.moduleCoverageLead: Distribution of verifications across the 10 modules of the IT Hygiene Guide.
overview.legendCv: Verified (CV) - rule whose compliance at the Standard level is observed by direct technical control on the workstation.
overview.legendPv: Partially verified (PV) - rule for which some aspects are observed; others require additional manual, contextual, or organisational evaluation.
overview.legendHp: Out of scope (HP) - organisational, contractual, or inter-machine architecture rule, not technically attestable on an isolated workstation.

summary.title: What was checked, and what was not
summary.cvBody: Compliance observed by a direct technical check.
summary.pvBody: Incomplete finding: probe unavailable, hardware absent, or human judgement required.
summary.keyFigureBody: Of the {evaluable} rules an endpoint audit can assess, {cvCount} are compliant and {pvCount} remain partial. Among the latter, {blindCount} are blind spots: the machine refused the query, or the probe does not cover it. A rule that cannot be assessed is not a compliant rule.
summary.noUrgent: No urgent measure was identified on this machine.

VIII.title: Keep the IS up to date

blind.act: Re-run the diagnostic with the necessary rights, or collect the missing data at its source.

defect.act: Correct the observed gap, then re-run the diagnostic to confirm it is resolved.

gap.act: Complete the check on the aspect left unevaluated, which is beyond what a workstation probe establishes.

partial.act: No immediate technical action. Document the element the probe cannot establish.

hp.act: No technical measure on the machine. This rule belongs to governance, to inter-machine architecture or to an organisational procedure, and must be handled as part of a separate organisational audit.

partial.act: Reconcile the local network map with the organisation's IT inventory and data classification.

blind.act: Re-run the diagnostic with local administrator rights, or extract the list of privileged accounts from the directory.

gap.act: Check the network access control configuration (802.1X) on the access switches.

blind.act: Re-run with local administrator rights to enumerate the accounts and confirm the separation between everyday and administrative use.

gap.act: Have the SMB share permissions reviewed and approved by the owner of the data concerned.

blind.act: Collect the applicable password policy (secpol.msc locally, or the GPO / Entra ID policy if the machine is managed).

partial.act: No action required. The finding is partial by nature: exhaustive coverage of credential storage vectors is beyond what a workstation probe can establish.

gap.act: Spot-check service accounts and device consoles for default credentials.
Enable Windows Hello for Business through Intune or group policy, then re-run the diagnostic.

ok.act: No action required. The Standard baseline is met. Autorun detection remains outside the current probe's coverage.

blind.act: Check the removable-device restriction policy and the AppLocker rules in the applicable GPO.

ok.act: Document the centralised management solution in use, which the probe does not identify.

gap.act: Assess the Reinforced firewall level (blocking inbound administration ports).

partial.act: Document the network segmentation architecture and the VLANs applicable to this machine.
Consider WPA3 at the next access-point refresh.

defect.act: Extend the audit to the remaining obsolete protocols (TLS 1.0/1.1, LLMNR, NetBIOS).

gap.act: Confirm whether a filtering gateway exists at network level; failing that, assess the case for DNS filtering.

blind.act: Re-run with local administrator rights to count the accounts holding administrative rights.

gap.act: Record the physical security measures applicable to mobile machines (cable lock, locked room, transport instructions).

ok.act: Verify that the BitLocker recovery key is backed up off the machine.

defect.act: Re-run the diagnostic with the VPN tunnel active in order to qualify the effective cryptographic configuration.
Re-run the failed updates through Windows Update, then verify that they applied.
Update the drivers flagged as obsolete from the manufacturer's catalogue.
Raise the logon audit policy to the level recommended by ANSSI (success and failure) through GPO.

ok.act: Place this diagnostic in a documented periodic cycle (frequency, scope, report recipient).

partial.act: Cross-reference the software inventory against the ANSSI catalogue of qualified products.

R1.name: Train operational teams in information system security

detail.hp_default: Operational team training - organisational measure, not technically observable on the workstation.

R2.name: Raise user awareness of basic IT security practices

R4.name: Identify the most sensitive information and servers and maintain a network diagram

detail.pv_local_only: Local network mapping observed (adapters, IP addresses, gateway). Global IS inventory and data classification remain outside the workstation scope.

R5.name: Maintain an exhaustive inventory of privileged accounts and keep it up to date

detail.pv_access_denied: Local administrator enumeration not available on this workstation (access denied). Manual verification required.

R6.name: Organise procedures for arrival, departure, and change of role of users

detail.hp_default: Arrival, departure, and role change procedures - HR and governance domain.

R7.name: Authorise network connection only to mastered equipment

detail.pv_joined: Workstation joined to a directory - join confirmed. Network admission control (802.1X) is not observable from the workstation.

R8.name: Identify each person accessing the system by name and distinguish user and administrator roles

detail.pv_guest_only: Guest account {guestState} (observed). Administrator account enumeration not available (access denied).

R9.name: Assign correct rights to sensitive resources of the information system

detail.pv_default: SMB share inventory captured as a snapshot. Access rights adequacy is not assessable without business context.

R10.name: Define and verify password selection and sizing rules

detail.pv_default: Local password policy is not extracted by current probes (G1 extension planned).

detail.pv_with_lsa: Credential Manager: {credInfo}. LSA (PPL) protection active. Coverage of storage vectors remains partial.
detail.pv_without_lsa: Credential Manager: {credInfo}. Coverage of storage vectors remains partial.

R12.name: Change default authentication elements on equipment and services

detail.pv_observed: Auto-logon: {autoLogonValue}. Default authentications of other components have not been tested.
detail.pv_default: No auto-logon detected in the registry. Default authentications of other components have not been tested.

detail.cv_full: Strong authentication configured: Windows Hello ({helloValue}), TPM operational.
detail.pv_tpm_ok: TPM 2.0 present and operational - strong authentication capability available. Effective Windows Hello configuration is not observed.

R14.name: Establish a minimum security level across the entire IT estate

detail.cv_default: Compliant at Standard level: local firewall active on all profiles, Microsoft Defender in real-time protection, BitLocker active on the system volume. Autorun element detection is not yet covered (G2 extension).
detail.pv_partial: Partial security baseline: {bits}. Standard level not fully achieved.

R15.name: Protect against threats related to removable media

detail.pv_default: USB restriction policy / AppLocker is not extracted by current probes (G3 extension planned).

R16.name: Use a centralised management tool to homogenise security policies

detail.cv_default: Workstation joined to a directory - centralised estate management confirmed, presumably via Microsoft Intune.

R17.name: Activate and configure the local firewall on workstations

detail.cv_all_active: All {count} Windows Firewall profiles (Domain, Private, Public) are active. Reinforced-level configuration (administration port blocking) is not evaluated.
detail.pv_partial: {passing}/{total} firewall profile(s) active. The firewall must be active on all profiles.

R18.name: Encrypt sensitive data transmitted over the Internet

detail.hp_default: In-transit data encryption - depends on application and messaging usage, outside the workstation scope.

R19.name: Segment the network and isolate zones of varying exposure

detail.pv_default: Local subnet and virtual adapters observed. Network segmentation architecture is outside the workstation scope.

R20.name: Ensure security of Wi-Fi access networks and separation of usages

detail.cv_wpa3: Wi-Fi connection encrypted with WPA3 - protocol compliant with current recommendations.
detail.cv_wpa2: Active Wi-Fi connection encrypted with WPA2-Personal. Encryption protocol compliant with current recommendations.
detail.pv_weak: Wi-Fi network with weak or absent encryption ({algorithm}). Migration to WPA2 or WPA3 recommended.
detail.pv_other: Wi-Fi observed: {value}. Encryption level to be confirmed.
detail.pv_no_wifi: No Wi-Fi connection observed at the time of the diagnostic.

R21.name: Use secure network protocols wherever they exist

detail.pv_smbv1_observed: SMBv1: {smbStatus}. Complete audit of obsolete protocols (TLS, LLMNR, NetBIOS) not yet implemented.
detail.pv_default: SMBv1 absent from the workstation. Complete audit of obsolete protocols not yet implemented.

R22.name: Establish a secure Internet access gateway

detail.pv_default: Internet access configuration: {proxyConfig}. URL filtering and secure DNS are not evaluated in detail.

R23.name: Isolate Internet-facing services from the rest of the information system

detail.hp_default: Isolation of exposed services - network architecture domain, outside the workstation scope.
Email security - server-side configuration, outside the workstation scope.

R25.name: Secure dedicated network interconnections with partners

detail.hp_default: Partner interconnections - inter-entity architecture, outside the workstation scope.

R26.name: Control and protect access to server rooms and technical premises

detail.hp_default: Physical access - organisational measure, outside the software scope.

R27.name: Forbid Internet access from workstations or servers used for IS administration

detail.hp_default: Administration workstation usage - architecture and usage policy, outside scope.

R28.name: Use a dedicated and isolated network for IS administration

detail.hp_default: Administration-dedicated network - network architecture, outside the workstation scope.

R29.name: Limit administration rights on workstations to strict operational need

detail.pv_uac_only: UAC active (policy: {uacPolicy}). Administrator account enumeration not available (access denied).
detail.pv_no_data: UAC state and number of administrators not extracted.

R30.name: Take physical security measures for mobile terminals

detail.pv_default: Hardware identified (portable workstation). Physical security measures are not technically observable.

R31.name: Encrypt sensitive data, particularly on potentially losable hardware

detail.cv_single_volume: System volume encrypted by BitLocker (AES encryption). On a portable workstation, the system volume is the primary data-loss vector.
detail.cv_all_volumes: All {total} detected volumes are encrypted by BitLocker (AES encryption).
detail.pv_partial: {on}/{total} volume(s) encrypted. Unencrypted volumes should be encrypted to limit risk in case of loss.

R32.name: Secure the network connection of workstations in mobile situations

detail.cv_connected: VPN tunnel active ({vpnInfo}). Mobile connection encrypted.
detail.pv_inactive: VPN client installed but inactive at the time of the diagnostic ({vpnInfo}). Cryptographic tunnel quality is not assessable offline.

R33.name: Adopt security policies dedicated to mobile terminals

detail.hp_default: Mobile terminal policy - concerns smartphones and tablets, outside the scope of a Windows workstation.

R34.name: Define a policy for updating IS components

detail.cv_with_failures: Windows Update operational. {count} update failure(s) detected in the last 30 days, to be retried.
detail.cv_clean: Windows Update operational - no recent failures detected.
detail.pv_no_data: Update policy not observed in probes.

R35.name: Anticipate end of maintenance of software and systems and limit software adhesions

detail.cv_obsolete_drivers: System under active support. {count} obsolete driver(s) detected, predating supported versions - replacement recommended.
detail.cv_clean: System and components under active support - no obsolete components detected.

R36.name: Activate and configure logs of the most important components

detail.cv_full: Active logging: connection auditing ({auditMode}), PowerShell Script Block Logging active.

detail.hp_default: Backup policy - infrastructure and procedures domain, outside the workstation scope.

R38.name: Carry out regular security controls and audits and apply associated corrective actions

detail.cv_default: Execution of {product} itself constitutes a regular technical audit control, directly responding to this measure.

R39.name: Designate an information system security contact

R40.name: Define a security incident management procedure

detail.hp_default: Formal risk analysis (EBIOS RM methodology) - methodological approach, outside the technical scope.

R42.name: Favour the use of ANSSI-qualified products and services

detail.pv_default: Software inventory captured as a snapshot. Automatic cross-referencing with the ANSSI catalogue of qualified products is not yet implemented (G7 extension).

conclusion.perimeterBody: This technical diagnostic automatically verifies {cvCount} ANSSI hygiene rules out of 42 at the local workstation level, and provides observational elements for {pvCount} additional rules. The remaining {hpCount} rules pertain to governance, inter-machine architecture, or organisational procedures that cannot be attested by a technical tool on an isolated workstation and require contextual evaluation.
conclusion.limit1: Informative diagnostic. This document constitutes neither an ANSSI certification nor an attestation within the meaning of the IT Hygiene Guide.
conclusion.limit2: ANSSI is the sole authority empowered to deliver official qualifications or certifications (see rule 42).
conclusion.limit3: Coverage limited to the audited workstation. Organisational evaluation (training, procedures, governance) is the subject of a separate audit.
conclusion.limit4: State observed at a given point in time. Any subsequent configuration change invalidates the finding.
conclusion.limit5: No ANSSI affiliation, accreditation, partnership, or approval. The term "ANSSI" is used in reference to the public document IT Hygiene Guide.
conclusion.integrityBody: SHA-256 imprint of the report content - any subsequent modification of this document would invalidate this signature:
conclusion.footerRef: Framework · ANSSI · IT Hygiene Guide · 42 rules · 2017
conclusion.title: Summary
conclusion.lead: This diagnostic establishes the compliance of {cvCount} rules out of 42 by direct technical check, documents {pvCount} partial findings and sets aside {hpCount} rules that do not belong to an endpoint audit.
conclusion.saysBody: The {cvCount} verified rules were verified by direct observation of the machine's state. These findings are reproducible: running the diagnostic again on an unchanged machine yields the same verdict and the same fingerprint.
conclusion.notSaysBody: {blindCount} rules could not be assessed for want of access or of a probe. They are neither compliant nor non-compliant: they are unknown, and the report says so rather than deciding. The measures aim first at clearing these blind spots, because an unknown costs an auditor more than an identified gap.
conclusion.otherBody: The {hpCount} out-of-scope rules are listed in the annex. No tool running on an isolated machine can attest to them; they appear in the report so that the framework stays complete.

spectrum.title: The 42 rules at a glance
spectrum.lead: Each square is a rule. The shape of this table is the diagnosis: what is established, what remains to be established, and what an endpoint audit cannot settle.
spectrum.whyLead: Why three states and not two.
spectrum.whyBody: A machine without a TPM cannot demonstrate hardware-backed authentication. Calling it compliant would be false; calling it non-compliant would suggest a defect that is not there. Partially verified names precisely what the tool could not establish — that is the information an auditor needs, and it is what a two-colour table destroys.

findings.title: Points of attention and measures
findings.lead: {findingCount} findings call for follow-up, out of {evaluable} assessable rules. Each carries the measure to take, who carries it out, and the estimated effort.

outOfScope.title: The {hpCount} rules an endpoint audit cannot settle
outOfScope.lead: These rules belong to the framework and were not assessed: they concern training, procedures, cross-machine architecture or governance. They are not defects. They call for a separate organisational audit.

attestation.title: Integrity and signatures
attestation.declarationBody: The undersigned technician attests to having run the {product} diagnostic on machine {hostname} on {dateHuman}, and that the findings reproduced here are those returned by the tool, unmodified.
attestation.extent: This document comprises {pages} pages numbered 1 to {pages}. Any missing or substituted page invalidates this attestation.
attestation.verdictHint: Independent of the report's language and layout. Sources and verification: page {page}.
attestation.writableNote: The {count} fields below are the only writable ones. Filling them changes neither the findings nor their fingerprint.
attestation.unknownContact: The report does not know the recipient: this field is left empty rather than filled with an invented value.

provenance.title: Where these findings come from
provenance.lead: A report issued today from a May collection describes the machine as it was in May. The observation date of each source appears below, with its gap to the issue date.
provenance.noSources: The collector recorded no sources. The findings cannot be dated.
provenance.staleNote: A gap of more than 30 days is flagged in red: the configuration may have changed since the collection. Re-run the probe concerned before concluding.
provenance.verdictBody: SHA-256 of the canonical list of verdicts — rule identifier, status, finding class, severity, source — sorted by rule number. It depends on neither the report's language nor its layout: two reports of the same machine in the same state carry the same fingerprint, in French as in English. A single changed verdict transforms it entirely. The pattern alongside is its visual rendering, comparable at a glance.
provenance.documentBody: SHA-256 of the HTML report as written to disk. It attests the file, not the verdicts: a layout correction changes it while the findings are identical. The signature fields are filled in after issue and do not enter the calculation.
provenance.signedCopyBody: The HTML file is the writable original; the PDF is its fixed impression. The document fingerprint above is computed on the report with the signature fields empty. To verify a signed copy: clear the eight marked fields, recompute the fingerprint, compare. The findings fingerprint verifies on either copy with no manipulation at all — that is the one that carries the substance.
provenance.engineBody: The 42 rules were evaluated by {product} {version}. A verdict depends on the version that produced it: a rule marked compliant under an earlier version does not assert the same thing. The findings fingerprint above is to be read together with this number.

classification.coverNote: This document enumerates the security weaknesses of a named machine. Its distribution should be limited to the commissioning party, the signing technician and those carrying out the measures.
